A malicious proposer exploited a mev-boost relay validation flaw on Ethereum mainnet on 2023-04-03 and reused revealed block contents to capture MEV from sandwich bots. Public loss estimates range from about $20M to just over $25M. The relay disclosed the block body after receiving a signed header without first requiring successful beacon-node publication or validating that the header represented a publishable block. That broke the commit-reveal boundary between proposer and builder and let a malicious proposer read the payload, suppress the canonical path with an invalid header, and rebuild a competing block from the revealed transactions.

A malicious Ethereum proposer exploited the mev-boost relay publication path on 3 April 2023, exposed private builder payloads from an invalid signed header, and stole about $20 million from sandwich bots. The relay released the block body after a proposer signed a header, even when local beacon nodes rejected that header as invalid. That broke the commit-reveal boundary and let the proposer read private builder payloads before publishing a competing block.
